title: The wrong interview
summary_es: Tom cuenta la mañana más embarazosa de su vida laboral: le hicieron la entrevista de otro candidato y no se atrevió a decirlo.
prediction_prompt: Have you ever been in an embarrassing situation at work or at school? What happened?

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I want to tell you about the most embarrassing morning of my working life.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: It was about six years ago. I'd applied for a job at a design company in Leeds.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: The interview was at nine, and I'd been preparing for it all week.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I'd even bought a new suit, which, looking back, was my first mistake.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Anyway, I arrived early, gave my name at reception, and was shown into a meeting room.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Two people were waiting. They shook my hand and started asking questions straight away.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: The first few were fine. Why did I want the job? What were my strengths?

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: But then the questions got strange. They asked how I would manage a team of forty people.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I'd never managed anyone in my life. I'd applied to be a junior designer!

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Still, I didn't want to look weak, so I made something up about listening and trust.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: They nodded. They wrote things down. One of them actually said, "Impressive."

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Then they asked about my ten years of experience in finance.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: At that point, I should have said something. Obviously. But I panicked.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I heard myself say, "Well, numbers have always been a passion of mine."

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: Numbers have never been a passion of mine. I can barely split a restaurant bill.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: After forty minutes, the door opened and a man in a much better suit came into the room.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: He said, "Sorry I'm late. I'm Thomas Reed, here for the finance director interview."

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: There was a very long silence. My name is Tom Reid. R, E, I, D.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: The receptionist had simply sent the wrong Reed to the wrong room.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: I apologised about nine times and was taken upstairs to my real interview, an hour late.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: By then I had nothing left to be nervous about, so I just told them the whole story.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: They laughed so much that one of them had to leave the room.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: And, believe it or not, I got the job. The design job, not the finance one.

segments.speaker: tom
segments.text: My boss still introduces me as "the man who nearly became our finance director".

connected_speech.explanation_es: *I'd* = *I had*. La *d* se pega a *applied*, y *for a* suena /fər ə/.
*I'd been* suena /aɪd bɪn/: es fácil no oír el *past perfect*.

connected_speech.explanation_es: *had* y *to* son débiles, y *left to* pierde una *t*.
